observation.visible_scene: A winding red plastic toy track (Hot Wheels style) is laid across grey sand, forming a U-shaped dip, a curved rise, and a long straight elevated section that bridges over a dug-out hole/trench. A small metallic silver ball rests on the track. A yellow object (a toy figure/connector) sits at the left end of the straight section. A second ladder-like track segment descends into the trench, and an additional curved track arc is visible at the top of the wider view.
visible_changes: The silver ball moves continuously along the red track: it starts at the low point of the U-curve, rolls up the right-hand ramp, passes around the upper bend, and then proceeds leftward along the straight bridge section, ending near the left end by the yellow object. This progression is shown by the ball changing its position relative to fixed track features (the curve, the bridge edge, the yellow object), not merely by camera shift.

The camera gradually zooms out and re-frames, revealing more of the layout over time: the trench/hole under the bridge, the descending track into the hole, the upper track arc, and the yellow object at the left all become visible that were partly or fully out of frame at the start.
The track, sand mounds, trench, descending track, and yellow object remain stationary throughout; only the ball changes position on the track.
outside_clip_unknowns: What set the ball in motion before frame 1 (the clip begins with the ball already moving).
Where the ball goes after frame 41 (it is still on the bridge approaching the yellow object; no stop, fall, or completion is shown).
Whether the ball ever travels onto the descending track into the hole or the upper arc track.
uncertain_details: Exact speed and acceleration of the ball along the track.
Whether the ball is rolling or sliding, and the role of the track's slope (gravity vs. push) is not determinable from the frames.
Precise identity/material of the yellow object and the ball (metallic appearance only).
The apparent leftward drift of the ball in some frames is partly confounded by the simultaneous camera zoom/pan, so per-frame pixel positions are not a pure measure of ball motion.
